title: Revithosoupa
subtitle: Greek chickpea soup with lemon and rosemary
excerpt: A simple, hearty soup of chickpeas simmered with onion, rosemary, and a generous pour of olive oil, finished with lemon juice. Filling, cheap, and very good the next day.
sourceNotes: Traditional Greek Monday soup, often made after a Sunday roast has depleted the pantry. Rosemary is used on the islands; mainland versions sometimes use bay and thyme instead.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze without the lemon juice. Add lemon to taste when reheating.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple easily in a large pot. Good for batch cooking and freezing in portions.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day once the chickpeas have absorbed more flavour. Reheat gently and add a fresh squeeze of lemon before serving.

content.text: Revithosoupa is a chickpea soup made rich with olive oil and bright with lemon. It uses tinned chickpeas for speed; dried soaked overnight also work well but need an extra hour of cooking. Do not skip the lemon at the end.
Heat 3 tablespoons of the olive oil in the large saucepan over a medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes until soft and translucent.
Add the garlic, rosemary, and bay leaves. Stir for 1 minute.
Tip in the chickpeas. Pour over the stock and stir to combine. Season with salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer and cook uncovered for 20 minutes. The chickpeas should be very soft and the broth slightly thickened.
Remove the rosemary sprigs and bay leaves. Use a potato masher to lightly crush about a quarter of the chickpeas against the side of the pan. This thickens the soup without pureeing it.
Stir in the remaining olive oil and the lemon juice. Taste and adjust seasoning.
Ladle into bowls and finish with a drizzle of olive oil and a grinding of black pepper.

items.symptom: The soup is thin and watery.
items.cause: The chickpeas were not crushed enough to release their starch, or too much stock was used.
items.fix: Crush more chickpeas against the side of the pan and simmer uncovered for another 10 minutes to reduce.

items.cause: Not enough lemon, or the olive oil was added too early and lost its freshness.
items.fix: Squeeze in more lemon juice and add a fresh drizzle of olive oil just before serving. Salt also lifts chickpea dishes significantly.

items.symptom: The rosemary flavour is too strong.
items.cause: The sprigs were left in too long.
items.fix: Remove rosemary after 15 minutes of simmering. A lighter hand with rosemary is easier to correct than one that has simmered too long.
